                            PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                         SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349

   JASON A. HOWTON'S SIXTH SET OF REQUESTS FOR INFORMATION
      TO ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA
        TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION REGARDING
               APPLICANTS' REBUTTAL TESTIMONY



Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6 and 16 TAC §22.141, Intervenor Jason A. Howton
hereby requests that Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission
Services Corporation provide the following information regarding Applicants’ rebuttal
testimony filed May 28, 2026.

INSTRUCTIONS
   1. Each RFI must be answered separately and completely. Objections must identify
   the specific ground and must be stated with particularity. A general or blanket
   objection is not sufficient.
   2. If any document is identified in a response, produce a copy of the document
   together with the response, unless already in evidence in this proceeding (in which
   case identify the item number and exhibit label).
   3. If the responding party lacks knowledge to respond to any part of an RFI, so state
   specifically and identify the person most likely to have the requested knowledge.
   4. Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6 and 16 TAC §22.141(c), responses to this Sixth
   Set are due within seven (7) working days of receipt. Objections are due within five
   (5) working days of receipt. RFIs received after 3:00 p.m. Central Time are deemed
   received the following business day.




RFI NO. 1
Witness: Jared Gurley, P.E., Item #5214, pp. 14–15; Exhibit JG-R3
Subject: Source data and route-specific applicability of economic benefit figures
   Mr. Gurley's rebuttal testimony states that the proposed 765-kV Import Path 2 project
   will provide '$890 million less in construction-related outage costs' and '$229 million
   more annual consumer energy cost savings' compared to a 345-kV alternative. (Item
   #5214, pp. 14–15; Exhibit JG-R3.)
    REQUEST (a): Produce the complete underlying economic analysis from the 2025
   Regional Transmission Plan (RTP) or any other source that generated the $890
   million and $229 million figures, including all assumptions, inputs, discount rates,
   load forecasts, and the geographic scope of the analysis.
   REQUEST (b): Identify whether either figure is a route-specific comparison between
   Route 894 and any specific alternative route (e.g., Route 899, Route 767), or whether
   both figures are system-level comparisons between 765-kV and 345-kV voltage
   classes that apply regardless of which specific route is selected.
   REQUEST (c): If neither figure is route-specific, confirm that Mr. Gurley's rebuttal
   testimony contains no economic analysis comparing Route 894 to any specific
   alternative route on any cost or benefit metric.
   REQUEST (d): Produce any sensitivity analysis or scenario modeling that shows how
   the $890 million and $229 million figures would change if a 765-kV route avoiding
   Links F20 and F23 (e.g., Route 899) were selected instead of Route 894.


RFI NO. 2
Witness: Russell Marusak, Item #5211, p. 8, Section IV; Environmental Assessment and
Routing Study App. F
Subject: Field verification records for habitable structure count on Route 894
   Mr. Marusak's rebuttal testimony states that 'Route 894 . . . has 85 directly affected
   habitable structures' within 500 feet of the route centerline. (Item #5211, p. 8.) His
   rebuttal also acknowledges that the Hoffman/Haufler structure was not captured on
   aerial imagery during initial review but was subsequently added following an
   intervenor challenge.
   REQUEST (a): Produce all field verification records, ground reconnaissance reports,
   and site visit logs prepared by Halff Associates, Kimley-Horn, or any other entity that
   physically visited or confirmed structures along Route 894 through Links F20 and
   F23 in the FM 2843/Cedar Valley corridor. Include dates, personnel, and structures
   visited.
   REQUEST (b): For each of the 85 counted structures within 500 feet of Route 894's
   centerline, identify: (i) whether the structure was field-verified by on-site personnel or
   identified solely through aerial/satellite imagery; (ii) the structure type (primary
   residence, commercial structure, barn, shed, outbuilding, other); and (iii) whether the
   structure was occupied on a daily or regular basis as of the date of the most recent
   survey.
    REQUEST (c): Produce the written methodology or protocol that Halff or Kimley-
   Horn used to determine which structures required field verification versus which were
   confirmed by aerial imagery alone, including the criteria for determining that field
   verification was 'practicable' under the methodology referenced in Footnote 2 of the
   Environmental Assessment and Routing Study.
   REQUEST (d): Identify any structures counted within 500 feet of Route 894's
   centerline that were built or rebuilt after the April 12, 2022 EF-3 tornado, and state
   whether post-tornado reconstruction in the FM 2843/Cedar Valley corridor was
   evaluated for inclusion in the structure count.


RFI NO. 3
Witness: Russell Marusak, Item #5211, p. 6, Section III
Subject: Scoring matrix and factor weights underlying the holistic route evaluation
   Mr. Marusak's rebuttal testimony states that 'the routing process adopts a holistic view
   of the proposed routing alternatives and the constraints identified throughout the
   study area.' (Item #5211, p. 6.) No scoring matrix, weighting rubric, or factor-by-
   factor analysis is produced or identified in his testimony.
   REQUEST (a): Produce the complete scoring matrix, evaluation rubric, or decision
   framework that Halff used to translate the individual routing factor measurements
   (habitable structures, compatible ROW, stream crossings, ESA acreage, cost, etc.)
   into a holistic route evaluation resulting in the recommendation of Route 894.
   REQUEST (b): For each routing factor listed in PURA §37.056(c)(4)(A)–(I) and 16
   TAC §25.101(b)(3), identify the specific weight, score, or priority assigned to that
   factor in Halff's evaluation methodology, or confirm that no quantitative weighting
   was applied to any factor.
   REQUEST (c): Produce any written comparison of Route 894 against Routes 899,
   767, 551, and 546 on each of the PURA §37.056(c)(4)(A)–(I) factors, identifying on
   which specific factors Route 894 was judged superior to those alternatives, and the
   data or analysis underlying each such judgment.
   REQUEST (d): Identify any Commission order, rule, or published guidance that
   authorizes or requires use of a 'holistic view' methodology rather than a documented
   factor-by-factor scoring process for evaluating transmission line route alternatives
   under 16 TAC §25.101.


RFI NO. 4
Witness: Russell Marusak, Item #5211, pp. 7–8, Section IV
 Subject: Legal standard applied to prudent avoidance determination
   Mr. Marusak's rebuttal testimony states that his 'understanding of the Commission's
   policy of prudent avoidance is that the process of routing a proposed transmission line
   should include consideration of routing options that will reasonably avoid population
   centers.' (Item #5211, pp. 7–8.) The text of 16 TAC §25.101(a)(6) defines prudent
   avoidance as 'the limiting of exposures to electric and magnetic fields that can be
   avoided with reasonable investments of money and effort.'
   REQUEST (a): Identify the Commission rule, order, or formal guidance that
   interprets 16 TAC §25.101(a)(6)'s requirement to 'limit' exposures as satisfied by
   'consideration of routing options,' or confirm that Mr. Marusak's characterization
   represents his personal understanding not derived from a specific Commission
   authority.
   REQUEST (b): Identify the specific quantitative reduction in EMF exposure —
   expressed in milligauss at habitable structures — that Applicants contend satisfies the
   'limiting of exposures' requirement for Route 894 through Links F20 and F23,
   compared to the next-best alternative route that avoids those links.
   REQUEST (c): Produce any analysis Halff conducted of whether Routes 767, 551,
   546, or 899 — each of which avoids Links F20 and F23 and is less expensive than
   Route 894 — constitute alternative routes that could limit EMF exposures at habitable
   structures in the FM 2843/Cedar Valley corridor 'with reasonable investments of
   money and effort' within the meaning of 16 TAC §25.101(a)(6).


RFI NO. 5
Witness: Russell Marusak, Item #5211, p. 4, Section II
Subject: Authority for 'standard industry practice' methodology assertion
   Mr. Marusak's rebuttal testimony states that 'Halff and Kimley-Horn's desktop
   analysis, in combination with ground and aerial reconnaissance surveys, is standard
   industry practice for transmission line projects in Texas prior to route finalization.'
   (Item #5211, p. 4.) No citation to a Commission rule, industry standard, or published
   guidance is provided.
   REQUEST (a): Identify the specific Commission rule, PURA provision, published
   industry standard (including the issuing organization and document title), or prior
   Commission order that Mr. Marusak relied upon in characterizing desktop analysis
   plus aerial reconnaissance as 'standard industry practice' for transmission line route
   selection in Texas.
    REQUEST (b): Mr. Marusak’s rebuttal testimony states that 'the Commission's final
   order will ensure that Applicants have the rights necessary to perform detailed field
   assessments of the approved route.' (Item #5211, p. 4.) Confirm whether detailed field
   assessments of Links F20 and F23 have been completed as of the date of these
   requests, and if not, produce the list of field assessment tasks that remain to be
   completed after route approval.


RFI NO. 6
Witness: Casey D. Petty, P.E., Item #5212, p. 5, ll. 3–6
Subject: Engineering and evidentiary basis for characterizing tornado impact as
'purported'
   The FM 2843/Cedar Valley corridor sits within a documented Central Texas tornado
   corridor that includes the May 27, 1997 F5 Jarrell tornado in adjacent Williamson
   County — the most violent tornado in Texas recorded history, with winds exceeding
   260 mph and 27 fatalities — and the April 12, 2022 EF-3 tornado with documented
   sustained winds of up to 165 mph that caused direct structural damage within the
   proposed F20 route alignment. Mr. Petty’s rebuttal testimony characterizes
   intervenors’ concerns about Links F20 and F23 as related to “the purported fall risk
   due to the occurrence of an EF-3 tornado in the area approximately four years ago.”
   (Item #5212, p. 5, ll. 3–6.)
   REQUEST (a): Produce all engineering studies, structural risk assessments,
   geotechnical analyses, or meteorological reports that Applicants conducted or
   commissioned regarding the April 12, 2022 EF-3 tornado’s impact on existing
   transmission structures in the FM 2843/Cedar Valley corridor, including any post-
   tornado inspection records for the existing transmission lines in that corridor.
   REQUEST (b): If no such studies or assessments were conducted, confirm that the
   word 'purported' in Mr. Petty's testimony reflects the absence of any Applicant-
   commissioned engineering analysis of the tornado's impact, not a conclusion derived
   from such analysis.
   REQUEST (c): Produce any analysis Applicants conducted of whether co-routing the
   proposed 765-kV line alongside existing transmission infrastructure in the FM
   2843/Cedar Valley corridor creates a single-event simultaneous outage risk,
   specifically in light of the corridor’s documented exposure to EF-3 tornado conditions
   with sustained winds of up to 165 mph and the broader tornado history of the Central
   Texas corridor in which Links F20 and F23 are located.
 RFI NO. 7
Witness: Dr. Edward P. Gelmann, Item #5208, p. 9, ll. 6–9
Subject: Source and conditions for right-of-way magnetic field estimate
   Dr. Gelmann's rebuttal testimony states: 'I understand that the magnetic fields
   associated with the Proposed Transmission Line Project are expected to range from
   approximately 160 to 350 milligauss within the right-of-way.' (Item #5208, p. 9, ll. 6–
   9.) No source, engineering exhibit, applicant filing, or calculation is cited for this
   figure.
   REQUEST (a): Identify the source, author, and date of the calculation, model, or
   engineering analysis that produced the 160–350 milligauss right-of-way estimate
   cited by Dr. Gelmann. Produce that calculation or analysis.
   REQUEST (b): Identify whether the 160–350 mG estimate reflects: (i) peak load
   conditions; (ii) design current; (iii) average load conditions; or (iv) some other basis,
   and produce the assumed current and voltage parameters used.
   REQUEST (c): Provide the calculated magnetic field levels at the following distances
   from the centerline of Route 894 through Link F20, under the same loading
   conditions: (i) edge of right-of-way; (ii) 500 feet; (iii) 700 feet; and (iv) 1,000 feet.
   REQUEST (d): Provide the corresponding electric field levels (in kV/m) at the same
   distances for the proposed 765-kV line operating at design voltage.


RFI NO. 8
Witness: Dr. Edward P. Gelmann, Item #5208, pp. 15–16; Exhibit EPG-R3; pp. 4–25
(entire testimony)
Subject: Omitted NIEHS precautionary siting recommendation and prudent avoidance
analysis
   Dr. Gelmann relies on the NIEHS EMF-RAPID publication (Exhibit EPG-R3, June
   2002) as his primary institutional authority. He quotes the NIEHS conclusion
   regarding weak laboratory evidence (Item #5208, pp. 15–16) but does not address a
   separate NIEHS recommendation contained in Exhibit EPG-R3, p. 52, that 'power
   companies and utilities continue siting power lines to reduce exposures.' Additionally,
   Dr. Gelmann's testimony does not contain the phrase 'prudent avoidance' and does not
   cite 16 TAC §25.101(a)(6).
   REQUEST (a): Confirm whether the language 'power companies and utilities
   continue siting power lines to reduce exposures' appears in Exhibit EPG-R3 at or near
   page 52. If it does, explain why Dr. Gelmann's testimony did not address that
    recommendation and whether Applicants contend their route selection for Route 894
   complies with it.
   REQUEST (b): State whether Dr. Gelmann's testimony constitutes Applicants'
   complete evidentiary showing on the prudent avoidance standard under 16 TAC
   §25.101(a)(6). If not, identify by item number and exhibit label the testimony or
   exhibit that contains Applicants' quantitative prudent avoidance analysis for Route
   894.
   REQUEST (c): Produce any analysis Dr. Gelmann or any other Applicant witness
   performed comparing the relative EMF exposure burden on habitable structures
   within 500 feet of Route 894's centerline versus Routes 899, 767, 551, or 546 —
   routes that avoid Links F20 and F23.
   REQUEST (d): Identify any systematic review or meta-analysis on ELF-EMF and
   childhood leukemia published after 2010 that Applicants considered in preparing Dr.
   Gelmann's testimony, or confirm that Exhibit EPG-R3 (June 2002) is the most recent
   systematic review relied upon.




Respectfully submitted,


/s/ Jason A. Howton
Intervenor, Pro Se
12808 FM 2843
Salado, Texas 76571
